name: Inverse Deformation Texture
definition: A technique used when forward free-form volumetric deformation is impossible. It constructs a grid (lattice) around the deformed volume in world space and associates each lattice point with texture coordinates in the unit fire volume to implicitly interpolate fire surfaces.
summary: Inverse Deformation Texture pre-computes world-space to unit-volume mappings in a lattice grid, enabling efficient real-time volumetric rendering by avoiding computationally prohibitive runtime inversion of complex deformation functions.
